tutorSurveys: Reviewed "friends of ten" and taught the "make a ten" strategy for addition.
AR is a very energetic kid, I should figure out some math games that help him move his body
For this session, I reviewed "friends of ten" and taught the "make a ten" strategy for addition. We played a card game to reinforce the "friends of ten."

DB was absent so the session was calmer. DB and DCG definitely have a relationship where DCG antagonizes and DB gives big reactions. Need to try and keep them working separately, maybe try to pair up DB w/JJ and DCG w/EM.
Reviewed “friends of ten” and taught “make a ten” addition strategy
10/10 session, need to make more games
Went over "friends of ten" and taught the "make a ten" strategy for addition. Played a card game to reinforce the friends of ten.
Ten snap is an absolute hit, I'll need to keep it around for sure. Card games seem to be a good way to go, so I should try to incorporate them into my sessions often.

DCS, EM, and DB were all distracting each other. DB expressed that he was bored multiple times, would throw small tantrums, and generally displayed behavior that indicated he was seeking attention. At one point, EM said that DB had touched one of his "private spots." This was brought to the attention of the ADA on site and is being handled according to the school's policies. JJ did not seem engaged, but she did not cause as many issues as EM, DB, and DCS. If this behavior continues into the next session I am going to have a conversation with Ms. Marabello and Ms. Quintavella.
Used a "friends of ten" version of snap to aid memorization, it was a hit!
Snap game was a hit, definitely going to use it with other groups to talk about friends of ten.

Everyone in this group is eager to participate, but also easy to sidetrack. All in all a good session, scholars showed a very solid grasp of addition with and without regrouping. I am going to move on to mental math strategies next.
May need to mix up the seating a bit or get different scholars to work together.

First session with MP, as she was sick for previous sessions. Quick lesson, was able to give her additional time to decorate her name plate. All the kids love to be helpers, which has made it very easy to get them to participate.

MP definitely the quietest of the group, will need to pay extra attention to ensure she is 1. paying attention and 2. participating. Warm calling would be a good option until we build her confidence. Scholars did relatively well with addition, but struggled in some cases with counting too high or too low (i.e. saying 8 + 5 is 12 instead of 13). The ‘make a ten’ strategy may be helpful for them.

This session served as an assessment of scholars' skills with addition. They showed proficiency in addition with and without regrouping. For the next session, I will focus on the mental math strategy "make a ten" to offer a new challenge and expand their thinking.
LC and LB tend to distract each other, I may have them sit across from each other rather than next to each other at the next session.

This group showed a solid understanding of addition with regrouping, so I attempted to pivot to the mental math "make a ten" strategy. The students seemed to struggle with it, so I am going to hit it again next session.
Scholars enjoyed i-Learn activity, but I need to figure out a different way to explain the make-a-ten strategy, as it did not seem to stick.

At the last session, I determined that these scholars had a solid grasp of addition. I asked what they would like to work on, and they said rounding. Rounding will definitely need to be drilled with this group, so that will be my primary focus in the coming weeks.

LD may need review of place values, seemed to struggle with ones' versus tens' place. We will still switch to subtraction for next week, but we're going to revisit and drill rounding with this group. I'll start with a review of place value for them, then we'll use that to lead into rounding.

SR is averse to taking academic challenge (requested an easier question to solve) and may need extra incentives to take risks. SH will participate when prompted, but not of his own accord. My focus with him should be building confidence.

Up the difficulty for the next session, these kids know thousands (maybe switch to mental math tricks?)
SR seems averse to taking academic challenges, may need extra incentives
SH will participate when prompted, but not of his own accord. Focus on building confidence.
Very easily distracted group
Focus on rounding for next session
May need to talk to SR privately about focus and interrupting. May emphasize that if her squishies and other toys distract her, that she will not be allowed to have them during the session.

Scholars showed a strong understanding of addition, including addition with regrouping. When I asked if they would prefer I focus on rounding or addition for the next session, the majority said rounding.
C & K have high potential to distract each other, maybe consider having them sit further apart? Or mix up the groups so that she works with L or D sometimes.

Scholars showed a solid grasp of addition of three-digit numbers without regrouping. AR in particular was very quick working through problems and eager to answer (had to be reminded to raise his hand). Scholars were engaged and enthusiastic. SC had a more difficult time, so I may need to give her extra support next session when we move on to addition with regrouping.

I need to be rehearsing and timing my lessons at home to make sure lessons aren't too short. Dot game was a good finishing activity, need to look for more games like that. I should expand on the number riddle concept to encourage them to practice addition and subtraction.

Request for slime and squishies, could be good incentive for early finishers. Could also use the squishy as a talking cue, whoever has the squishy talks and everyone else is silent.
